source.section: Worksheet Step 1 lines 1-7, Step 2 lines 8-13 and instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1s; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 73,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 = 107,000.00. Federal taxable income = 107,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 89,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 107,000.00. Line 1s, Social Security worksheet: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70). Line 3 federal AGI 107,000.00; line 4 Single; line 5 born on or before 03/01/1959: yes; line 6 107,000.00; line 7 107,000.00 less than 107,000.00: no. STOP: not eligible; modification 0.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 107,000.00 + (0.00) = 107,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 107,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Single). Line 5 = 107,000.00 - 10,900.00 = 96,100.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 96,100.00 - 5,100.00 = 91,000.00. Line 8 tax on 91,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 79,900.00 x 0.0375 = 2996.2500 + 11,100.00 x 0.0475 = 527.250000 = 3,523.50. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 3,523.50. Note: Exactly 107,000: worksheet line 7 asks 'less than', so the answer is no and the worksheet stops.
